profile.campus: Digital Fortress Portland/Beaverton cluster (acquired from Atmosera, Jan 2021, with PTL and PTL3)
profile.address: 9705, Southwest Sunshine Court, Quad 217 Corporate Center, Raleigh West, Denney Whitford/Raleigh West, Beaverton, Washington County, Oregon, 97005
profile.reading:
Digital Fortress - Portland 2, known in the operator's own materials as PTL2, is a colocation data center at 9705 Southwest Sunshine Court in Beaverton, Oregon, about fifteen minutes from downtown Portland by the operator's own account. It is operated by Digital Fortress, Inc, a privately held colocation company that states on its own site it was founded in 2003 and is headquartered in Seattle, Washington. Digital Fortress runs two other buildings on the same short cul-de-sac and one further site downtown, together forming its Portland-area cluster, and the company's own materials describe PTL2 as offering true redundancy and replication between the three sites.

The Beaverton buildings did not start life as Digital Fortress properties. Digital Fortress announced on January 19, 2021 that it had acquired the colocation business of Atmosera, Inc, picking up three Portland-area facilities, one downtown and two in Beaverton, along with more than 100 existing colocation customers. That lineage runs further back still. EasyStreet Online Services, a Portland-based internet and managed-services provider that by 2013 had operated for roughly two decades, merged that year with Infinity Internet in a deal backed by a strategic investment from Seaport Capital and additional capital from Goldman Sachs, and EasyStreet's own leadership described the combined company as running enterprise-class data centers in both Beaverton and downtown Portland. Public sources do not specify whether it was this building or its Sunshine Court neighbor that carried EasyStreet's original data center floor before the Atmosera and Digital Fortress transitions, so that detail is left open here rather than guessed at.

On power, Digital Fortress's own PTL2 facility page states 1.2 megawatts of available IT power capacity, an N+1 concurrently maintainable design, and about 3,500 square feet of technical space cooled by 160 tons of direct expansion equipment. That IT figure comes labeled for this specific building and is the only one of the four power figures this record can responsibly fill in. No standby generator rating, onsite generation figure, or utility feed capacity is published anywhere in the operator's own materials for PTL2 specifically, so those remain unset rather than borrowed from the neighboring PTL3 building, which separately advertises three diesel generators and 1.5 megawatts of IT capacity of its own. The facility also markets itself as carrier neutral with sixteen fiber carriers on site, membership in the Northwest Access Exchange, and a fiber link toward the Pittock Block and Seattle Internet Exchange that the operator credits with reaching seven subsea cable systems, positioning a comparatively small Beaverton building as unusually well connected for its size.

Unlike the hyperscale campuses that have made neighboring Hillsboro a national data center story, this building sits in Beaverton, a separate Washington County city with its own planning and taxing authority. Washington County's own published Strategic Investment Program agreement list names only two projects, an Intel agreement from 2014 and a proposed Lam Research agreement from 2026, with no data center specific SIP deal listed for any Beaverton or Hillsboro colocation property, and Hillsboro's own accounting of data center tax abatements applies to sites within Hillsboro city limits, not Beaverton. Nothing found in county, city, or press records ties PTL2 to any specific property tax abatement, and Oregon law shields the identities of enterprise zone applicants in any case, so that question is left unresolved rather than assumed.

reading.body:
Digital Fortress Portland 2 is a 3,500 square foot colocation facility in Beaverton, Oregon with 1.2 megawatts of available IT capacity on an N+1 redundant power configuration and 160 tons of direct expansion cooling. At a typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, 1.2 megawatts of IT load translates to roughly 30 racks, though this facility appears designed for general colocation rather than large-scale GPU clusters. The operator acquired this building and two neighboring Portland facilities from Atmosera in January 2021 and transferred more than 100 colocation customers to Digital Fortress, indicating an active hosting business rather than a greenfield development.

The facility holds SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II certifications and connects to 16 fiber optic carriers and seven subsea cables through membership in the Northwest Access Exchange and the Seattle Internet Exchange. These certifications qualify it for regulated workloads and its carrier count suggests general-purpose colocation connectivity rather than a dedicated hyperscaler backbone. The facility does not publish its total capacity figure, preventing direct assessment of its actual density or utilization.

Portland 2 ranks ninth in published capacity across Oregon, though this ranking reflects only eight facilities in the state that publish megawatt figures out of 133 mapped data centers. Oregon's eight published facilities total 156.6 megawatts, placing this facility at less than 1% of the state's disclosed capacity. The facility is one of three adjacent buildings Digital Fortress operates in the Portland area, but the state context does not distinguish capacity or utilization across these properties.
